newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Sept 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Sept 6.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indonesian political and business stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Jakarta. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (6221) 384-6364. Fax: (6221) 344-8404.

There is no chance of an out-of-court settlement between Megawati Sukarnoputri and Surjadi -- rival contenders for the leadership of the Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI). Megawati's lawyer RO Tambunan made the remark on Thursday after demanding a court order to stop Surjadi's faction from occupying the party's headquarters.

Lippo Bank, Lippo Securities and Lippo Life may re-evaluate their proposal for a cross-holding of shares in the three firms after earlier reports that the capital market supervisory agency (Bapapem) was likely to be against the proposal.

The directors-general of Customs from the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) finalised an agreement on customs cooperation on Thursday. They stated their commitment to removing barriers to trade in the region in preperation for the implementation of the ASEAN Free Trade Area (AFTA).
A demonstration by 50 Islamic students was held outside the U.S. embassy yesterday in protest of the recent bombing raids over Iraq.
